rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan readers other than Asim use masculine yanfada; the other readers use feminine tanfada.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم أن ينفد بالياء والباقون تنفد بالتاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The feminine reading is better because its grammatical subject is feminine, though masculine agreement is also acceptable for a non-natural feminine.
rows.anchor: تنفد بالتاء أحسن لأن المسند إليه للفعل مؤنث والمذكر حسن أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد وسليمان التيمي
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading has madadan in place of madada.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد وسليمان التيمي ولو جئنا بمثله مدادا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Madadan can be a circumstantial accusative or a cognate accusative supplied by an implied verb meaning to add.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ مددا فهو منصوب على الحال كما يقال جئتك بزيد عونا لك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Madadan is a specification meaning an amount of ink, like saying someone has an equal number of slaves or dates.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو منصوب على التمييز ومن قال جئنا بمثله مدادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaws is a garden combining dates, flowers, and other delights; al-Zajjaj defines it as a garden gathering the best features of every garden.
rows.anchor: الفردوس البستان الذي يجتمع فيه التمر والزهر وسائر ما يمتع ويلذ

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say Firdaws means valleys producing many kinds of plants and that the word entered Arabic from Persian.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم إن الفردوس الأودية التي تنبت ضروبا من النبت وقالوا هو بالرومية منقول إلى لفظ العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit is cited as the only Arabic poet in whom Firdaws was found, describing the monotheist reward as an abiding garden.
rows.anchor: فإن ثواب الله كل موحد جنان من الفردوس فيها يخلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawal means moving away from a place; it can also mean a stratagem or a transfer, according to al-Azhari and Ibn al-Arabi.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الحول أيضا الحيلة. وقيل: إن الحول بمعنى التحويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midad is writing ink, while madad is an extension arriving successively; kalima can mean one utterance or a poem as one unit of speech.
rows.anchor: والمداد التي يكتب به والمدد المصدر وهو مجيء شيء بعد شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can use a small plural for a large number and vice versa; the commentary cites the many rooms of Paradise and divine ranks as examples.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن العرب تستغني بالجمع القليل عن الجمع الكثير وبالكثير عن القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hassan’s line uses small plurals for abundant shields and swords; Abu Ali rejects the story that al-Nabigha criticized him for it as unreliable.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو علي الفارسي ينكر الحكاية التي تروى عن النابغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If nuzul means a dwelling, it is the predicate of kana; if it means hospitality, an omitted phrase supplies the fruits and bliss offered to guests.
rows.anchor: إن جعلت نزلا لمعنى المنزل فهو خبر كان على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul can also be the plural of nazil, an accusative circumstantial phrase referring to the pronoun in lahum.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نزلا جمع نازل فيكون نصبا على الحال

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Kana describes what was already decreed in God's knowledge before the believers were created.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كان أنه كان في علم الله تعالى قبل أن يخلقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in falyamal may retain its original kasra or be silent; kasra is original but heavier to pronounce.
rows.anchor: وقوله فليعمل يجوز كسر اللام وإسكانها والأصل الكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers trusted God and His messenger; their allotted Firdaws is the finest, central, highest part of Paradise, according to Qatada.
rows.anchor: كان في حكم الله وعلمه لهم بساتين الفردوس وهو أطيب موضع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Firdaws is also described as a garden whose trees interlace densely.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الجنة الملتفة الأشجار عن قتادة.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Another view identifies Firdaws as the garden containing grapevines.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو البستان الذي فيه الأعناب عن كعب

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت عن النبي
rows.claim: A report says Paradise has one hundred levels, each separated by the distance between heaven and earth; Firdaws is highest, its rivers spring from it, and believers should ask for it.
rows.anchor: الجنة مائة درجة ما بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض الفردوس أعلاها درجة منها تفجر أنهار الجنة الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul means a dwelling and refuge; another gloss is the place where one alights.
rows.anchor: أي منزلا ومأوى. وقيل: ذات نزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers remain in Paradise permanently and seek no change of residence because it is delightful and fulfills their wishes.
rows.anchor: لا يطلبون عن تلك الجنات تحولا إلى موضع آخر لطيبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea, meaning the sea’s water, is imagined as ink for recording all that God can say, decree, and command.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم الجنس أي لو كان البحر بمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes God's words as what He promises the rewarded and threatens the punished; this is attributed to Abu Muslim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالكلمات ما وعد لأهل الثواب وأوعد لأهل العقاب عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses understand the words as God's capacities, wisdom, and marvels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن كلماته المراد بها مقدوراته وحكمته وعجائبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the words as their meanings and benefits, including the Quran and earlier books, not the already-written words themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بكلمات ربي معاني كلمات ربي وفوائدها وهي القرآن وسائر كتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even another sea brought as a supplement would not exhaust God's words; midad is called ink because it supplies the writer.
rows.anchor: ولو جئنا بمثل البحر مددا له أي عونا وزيادة لما نفد ذلك

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: After Quran 17:85 was revealed, Jews claimed extensive knowledge because of the Torah, and this verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال لما نزل قوله:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God's words mean knowledge that cannot be comprehended or counted; the commentary compares this with the image of every earthly tree becoming pens.
rows.anchor: أراد بالكلمات العلم فإنه لا يدرك ولا يحصى ونظيره ولو أن ما في الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God taught the Prophet humility: he is human like others, honored by revelation, with no distinction or knowledge beyond what God gives.
rows.anchor: علم الله نبيه التواضع لئلا يزهى على خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting the Lord means hoping for His reward, affirming resurrection, and expecting to stand before Him.
rows.anchor: يطمع في لقاء ثواب ربه ويأمله ويقر بالبعث إليه والوقوف بين يديه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Meeting the Lord can mean fearing the punishment awaiting the person.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه فمن كان يخشى لقاء عقاب ربه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope in this verse can encompass both fear and expectation, as a cited poem says not every hoped-for good or evil occurs.
rows.anchor: إن الرجاء يشتمل على كلا المعنيين الخوف والأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous deed is one performed sincerely for God as an act of devotion.
rows.anchor: أي خالصا لله تعالى يتقرب به إليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The prohibition on associating anyone in worship includes angels, humans, stones, and trees.
rows.anchor: غيره من ملك أو بشر أو حجر أو شجر عن الحسن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The phrase can mean not displaying worship to gain anyone’s approval.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا يرائي في عبادته أحدا عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The verse followed a man’s question: he gave charity and maintained kinship for God, but felt pleased when people praised him.
rows.anchor: فنزلت الآية

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The wording targets deeds done for God while seeking praise; giving charity through another distributor can prevent recipients from exalting the donor.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل ولا يشرك به لأنه أراد العمل الذي يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه

rows.speaker: النبي عن الله
rows.claim: A sacred report says God rejects a deed shared with another; the author notes that Muslim included it in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: أنا أغنى الشركاء عن الشرك فمن عمل عملا أشرك فيه غيري

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت وشداد بن أوس عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said ostentatious prayer or fasting is association, then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: من صلى صلاة يرائي بها فقد أشرك ومن صام صوما يرائي به فقد أشرك

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: When he saw a servant pour water for al-Mamun’s ablution, he cited this verse; al-Mamun dismissed the servant and finished washing himself.
rows.anchor: فصرف المأمون الغلام وتولى إتمام وضوئه بنفسه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say this was the last verse revealed from the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هذه الآية آخر آية نزلت من القرآن.

rows.speaker: علي عن عيسى بن عبد الله عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali promises light from the sleeper’s resting place toward the Kaaba for reciting this passage, extending to Jerusalem for someone in the Sacred Precinct.
rows.anchor: إلا كان له نورا في مضجعه إلى بيت الله الحرام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Reciting the end of al-Kahf before sleep is said to wake a person at the hour they choose.
rows.anchor: ما من أحد يقرأ آخر الكهف عند النوم إلا يتيقظ في الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea comparison follows the commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats by showing God's limitless power; people must obey, trust promises, and fear threats.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم الأمر والنهي والوعد والوعيد وعقب ذلك سبحانه ببيان أن مقدوراته لا تتناهى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads the letters with imala on ha and an open ya.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو كهيعص بإمالة ها وفتح يا

rows.speaker: ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان وحمزة وخلف
rows.claim: These readers open ha and use imala on ya; al-Kisai uses imala on both, and the remaining named transmissions use both open vowels.
rows.anchor: برواية ابن ذكوان وحمزة وخلف بفتح ها وإمالة يا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ali says imala is possible because the separated letters are names of sounds, not particles; nouns can take imala and inflection when discussed as names.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي القول في إمالة هذه الحروف أنها لا تمتنع لأنها ليست بحروف معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers generally conceal the n of ayn, while Hafs pronounces it clearly.
rows.anchor: وكلهم أخفى نون عين إلا حفصا فإنه بين النون

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Clear n before a following oral consonant is normally ungrammatical, but detached letter names are paused and therefore should be pronounced clearly.
rows.anchor: وبيان النون مع حروف الفم لحن إلا أن هذه الحروف تجري على الوقف

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says clarifying the n is better Arabic because letter names, like number names, are separate; most readers nonetheless conceal it.
rows.anchor: التبيين يعني تبيين النون أجود في العربية لأن حروف الهجاء والعدد يفصل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: They read yarithni and yarith with jussive endings; the other readers use indicative endings.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي يرثني ويرث بالجزم فيهما والباقون بالرفع فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indicative treats the inheriting child as a descriptive attribute of the requested heir, not as a condition; the jussive makes inheritance a condition answering the prayer.
rows.anchor: وليس المعنى على الجزاء أي إن وهبته يرث

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: The variant yarithuni warithun uses tajrid, extracting a second description from the same heir, as in saying someone has a house of eternity that is itself that house.
rows.anchor: وهي نفسها دار الخلد فكأنه جرد من الدار دارا وعليه قول الأخطل:

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal’s verse similarly presents Musab himself as the ashath, illustrating the same Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: بنزوة لص بعدما مر مصعب بأشعث لا يفلى ولا هو يقمل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The reading dhikru rahmati rabbika treats the recited Quran beginning with these letters as a mention of the Lord’s mercy.
rows.anchor: فإن فاعل ذكر ضمير ما تقدم أي هذا المتلو من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikru rahmati rabbika may be parsed as a nominal sentence: the Quran is a mention of the Lord’s mercy, with Zakariya as the object of mercy and a clarifying apposition.
rows.anchor: أي هذا القرآن ذكر رحمة ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khift al-mawali can mean that Zakariya’s cousins and family were few; min warai means those he expects to succeed him, expressed as a present expectation.
rows.anchor: ومن قال خفت الموالي فمعناه قل بنو عمي وأهلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahn means weakness and loss of strength; اشتعل الرأس شيبا is a vivid metaphor for gray hair spreading like firelight.
rows.anchor: الوهن الضعف ونقصان القوة يقال وهن يهن وهنا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The phrase about the head catching fire is an established expression for someone whose hair has become very gray; Labid supplies a poetic example.
rows.anchor: يقال للشيب إذا كثر جدا قد اشتعل رأس فلان وأنشد للبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a request for an action from the one invoked, and its counterpart is a response, just as obedience answers a command.
rows.anchor: والدعاء طلب الفعل من المدعو وفي مقابلته الإجابة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Mawla has eight lexical senses: patron, freed person or former owner, ally, one with priority, cousin, neighbor, in-law, and confederate.
rows.anchor: المولى في اللغة ينقسم على ثمانية أقسام المنعم المعتق والمنعم عليه المعتق

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal’s line uses mawla in the sense of protector or the one most entitled to something.
rows.anchor: فأصبحت مولاها من الناس بعده وأحرى قريش أن تهاب

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: The continuation of al-Akhtal’s poem illustrates the lexical discussion of mawali and their loyalty to their own people.
rows.anchor: لا جد إلا صغير بعد محتقر لم يأشروا فيه إذ كانوا مواليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqir describes a woman unable to bear children and a man who cannot father them; the root also denotes a bodily wound or cutting a horse’s legs.
rows.anchor: والعاقر المرأة التي لا تلد يقال امرأة عاقر ورجل عاقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqir may derive from a deficiency in original constitution, whether caused by injury or inability to give birth.
rows.anchor: والعقر في البدن الجرح ومنه أخذ العاقر لأنه نقص أصل الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaala has four uses: create something, transform it, assign a status or judgment, or cause someone to act by ordering or prompting them.
rows.anchor: والجعل على أربعة أقسام بمعنى الإحداث كقولهم جعل البناء

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith states that the best prayer is quiet and the best provision is what suffices.
rows.anchor: خير الدعاء الخفي وخير الرزق ما يكفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya may have concealed his prayer to avoid people mocking an elderly man for asking for a child.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما أخفاه لئلا يهزأ به الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya says his bones have weakened because bones remain firm longer than flesh and nerves; another explanation links the complaint to weakness of grasp.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضاف الوهن إلى العظم لأن العظم مع صلابته إذا ضعف

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The spreading gray hair is described as a warning of death.
rows.anchor: معناه أن الشيب قد عم الرأس وهو نذير الموت عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Another reading of the metaphor is that gray hair shines across Zakariya’s head because it has become abundant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه تلألأ الشيب في رأسي لكثرته عن ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya presents his physical state in humility rather than merely reporting it, and recalls that earlier prayers were never disappointed.
rows.anchor: وصف حاله خضوعا وتذللا لا تعريفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaki in this context means exhausting oneself in a request without obtaining what one sought; Zakariya asks not to be denied now.
rows.anchor: يقال شقي فلان بحاجته إذا تعب بسببها ولم يحصل مطلوبه منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-mawali means the distant kindred, or kalala.
rows.anchor: { وإني خفت الموالي } وهم الكلالة عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-mawali means the agnatic clan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العصبة عن مجاهد.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-mawali refers to paternal uncles and cousins; other reported views identify cousins, immoral Israelite cousins, or heirs.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم العمومة وبنو العم عن أبي جعفر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Yaqub is identified as the son of Mathan, brother of Imran, Mary’s father; another genealogy traces him to Isaac and Abraham through Solomon and Judah.
rows.anchor: وهو يعقوب بن ماثان وأخوه عمران بن ماثان أبو مريم عن الكلبي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: One view assigns Zakariya’s own inheritance to property and the inheritance from Jacob’s family to prophethood.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه يرثني مالي ويرث من آل يعقوب النبوة عن أبي صالح

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another view understands both inheritances as prophethood, Zakariya’s and that of Jacob’s family.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يرث نبوتي ونبوة آل يعقوب عن الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school argues that inheritance here is property: the literal legal meaning concerns what passes to heirs, and no evidence requires a metaphor for knowledge or prophethood.
rows.anchor: لفظ الميراث في اللغة والشريعة لا يطلق إلا على ما ينتقل من الموروث إلى الوارث

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The request that the heir be pleasing supports material inheritance, since prophethood already entails uprightness; Zakariya feared immoral relatives would waste his property in sin.
rows.anchor: وإنما يطلب وارثا لأجل خوفه ولا يليق خوفه منهم إلا بالمال دون النبوة

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read ʿitiyyan, ʿasiyyan, jithiyyan, and bukiyyan with kasra at the beginning; Hafs does likewise except that he uses damma in bukiyyan.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي عتيا وصليا وجثيا وبكيا بكسر أوائلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains the kasra in these forms through patterns in broken plurals and verbal nouns: weak final waw can shift to ya, with related forms analogically following.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: اعلم أن ما كان على فعول كان على ضربين أحدهما: أن يكون جمعا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read We created you in the plural; the rest read I created you in the singular.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي خلقناك والباقون خلقتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular reading agrees with the preceding speech your Lord said; the plural reading fits what follows and the plural speaker elsewhere in the passage.
rows.anchor: حجة من قال قد خلقتك إن قبله قال ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A weak final waw in these plurals changes to ya; Abu Ali illustrates the pattern with ḥaqw/ḥaqī and ʿaṣā/ʿaṣī.
rows.anchor: فما كانت اللام منه واوا من هذه الجموع قلبت إلى الياء وذلك نحو حقو وحقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from singular to plural has a Quranic parallel: God says He carried His servant on the night journey and then says We gave Moses the Book.
rows.anchor:
سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده
[الإسراء: 1] ثم قال
وآتينا موسى الكتاب
[الإسراء: 2]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismuhu Yahya is a nominal clause modifying boy; kathalika has an omitted subject meaning the matter is as announced; lam tak drops its frequent final n.
rows.anchor: { اسمه يحيى } جملة اسمية مجرورة الموضع صفة الغلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An sabbihu can mean an explanatory that is, or a reduced annahu with an unexpressed subject; the commentary cites parallel Quranic constructions.
rows.anchor: { أن سبحوا } يجوز أن يكون التقدير أي سبحوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukratan and ʿashiyyan are adverbial expressions of time.
rows.anchor: وبكرة وعشيا منصوبان على الظرف

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: No one before Yahya had borne his name; the author calls this a distinction because God named him and chose a name not previously used.
rows.anchor: لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: He says Husayn too had no namesake; the sky was red at dawn and dusk for forty mornings, and the killers of Yahya and Husayn were illegitimate.
rows.anchor: لم يكن له من قبل سميا ولم تبك السماء إلا عليهما أربعين صباحا

rows.speaker: علي بن زيد عن علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: While travelling with Husayn, Ali Zayn al-Abidin says Husayn mentioned Yahya at every stop and recalled that Yahya’s head was presented to an adulteress.
rows.anchor: ما نزل منزلا ولا ارتحل منه إلا ذكر يحيى بن زكريا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another explanation of samiyyan is someone equal to Yahya, linked to the question whether God has any namesake in 19:65.
rows.anchor: أي مثلا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Zakariya asks whether God will restore their youth or grant them a child while both are elderly.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن إنما قال ذلك على جهة الاستخبار أي أتعيدنا شابين

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: ʿAtiyya means old age has dried and hardened the body and thinned the bones; Qatada says Zakariya was over ninety.
rows.anchor: وقد بلغت من كبر السن إلى حال اليبس والجفاف ونحول العظم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God can restore Zakariya’s strength for intercourse and open his wife’s womb to conceive.
rows.anchor: أرد عليك قوتك حتى تقوى على الجماع وافتق رحم امرأتك بالولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making an infertile wife able to conceive is easier to imagine than creating Zakariya from nothing in the first place.
rows.anchor: فإزالة عقر زوجتك وإزالة ما يمنع قبول الولد أيسر في الاعتبار

rows.speaker: الحكم بن عيينة عن أبي جعفر
rows.claim: Yahya was born five years after the divine announcement to Zakariya.
rows.anchor: إنما ولد يحيى بعد البشارة له من الله بخمس سنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Zakariya’s tongue was held for three days without illness while he remained healthy.
rows.anchor: اعتقل لسانه من غير مرض ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: His speech was restrained without injury or muteness: he could recite the Psalms, pray, and glorify God but not speak to people, an extraordinary sign.
rows.anchor: اعتقل لسانه من غير بأس ولا خرس فإنه كان يقرأ الزبور

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The mihrab was Zakariya’s prayer place; it is named as such because one facing it battles Satan during prayer.
rows.anchor: من مصلاه عن ابن زيد وسمي المحراب محرابا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Zakariya communicated by gestures, or according to another report, wrote his instruction on the ground.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كتب لهم في الأرض عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Subbihu means perform the morning and evening prayers; prayer is called glorification because it contains tasbih, though another view takes it as glorification itself.
rows.anchor: أي صلوه بكرة وعشيا عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanan fundamentally means mercy or tenderness; the commentary illustrates it with lines from Imru al-Qays, another poet, Tarafa, and al-Hutayia.
rows.anchor: أصل الحنان الرحمة يقال حنانك وحنانيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbar describes someone who recognizes no rights over himself and can also describe a palm tree whose fruit is beyond reach.
rows.anchor: والجبار الذي لا يرى لأحد عليه حقا وفيه جبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi in bi-quwwa marks a circumstantial state: Yahya is to take the Book earnestly and diligently.
rows.anchor: الباء في موضع الحال أي خذ الكتاب مجدا مجتهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative compresses the grant of Yahya: God gave him understanding and reason, then commanded him to take the Torah with strength God supplied.
rows.anchor: ها هنا اختصار عجيب تقديره فوهبنا له يحيى وأعطيناه الفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-quwwa can also mean with serious resolve and firm determination to follow the Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه بجد وصحة عزيمة على القيام بما فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Hukm means prophethood granted to Yahya as a child of three years.
rows.anchor: أي آتيناه النبوة في حال صباه وهو ابن ثلاث سنين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي بن أسباط عن أبي جعفر
rows.claim: Imam Baqir, then five, says God’s granting of imamate can occur in childhood just as prophecy was granted to Yahya as a child.
rows.anchor: إن الله قد أخذ في الإمامة كما أخذ في النبوة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Hukm may mean understanding the Book; Maʿmar reports that when boys invited Yahya to play, he answered that they were not created for play.
rows.anchor: قال إن الصبيان قالوا ليحيى اذهب بنا لنلعب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Zakah can mean obedience to God and sincerity.
rows.anchor: يعني بالزكاة طاعة الله والإخلاص عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Zakah may be a gift of charity from God to Yahya’s parents.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وصدقة تصدق الله به على أبويه عن الكلبي.

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Another view says God purified Yahya with good praise, as witnesses purify a person by their testimony.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وزكيناه بحسن الثناء عليه كما يزكي الشهود الإنسان عن الجبائي.

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Yahya was so pious that he neither committed nor intended a sin.
rows.anchor: وكان من تقواه أنه لم يعمل خطيئة ولم يهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asiyya is an active participle meaning disobedient to his Lord.
rows.anchor: { عصيا } أي عاصيا لربه فعيل بمعنى فاعل.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jabbar may mean someone who kills or strikes in anger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الجبار الذي يقتل ويضرب على الغضب عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Peace can mean safety and protection from God; Yahya is protected from Satan at birth, worldly trials and grave punishment at death, and the terror of resurrection and Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وسلامة وأمان له منا عن الكلبي ومعناه سلامة وأمن له يوم ولد من عبث الشيطان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God attributes Yahya’s purity to Himself because divine لطف guided him, especially in childhood, and enabled his obedience.
rows.anchor: أنه إنما صار كذلك بإلطاف من الله لا سيما في تلك الحالة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: The greeting of peace on the three days is from God.
rows.anchor: أي سلام عليه منا في هذه الأيام عن عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayyan emphasizes that Yahya will truly be raised alive.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال حيا تأكيدا لقوله: { يبعث }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Yahya is raised with the martyrs because they are described as alive.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني أنه يبعث مع الشهداء لأنهم وصفوا بأنهم أحياء

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan says the three most lonely moments are birth, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الإنسان في ثلاثة مواطن يوم ولد

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش وقالون ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read li-yahab with third-person y; the others read li-ahab with first-person hamza, and Ubay and Ibn Masud also have the y form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وورش وقالون برواية الحلواني ويعقوب ليهب بالياء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: In li-ahab the angel ascribes the gift to himself as a messenger, though God is the actual giver; li-yahab makes God the explicit subject.
rows.anchor: حجة من قال لأهب فأسند الفعل إلى المتكلم والهبة لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh is throwing away; intibadh is withdrawing by setting oneself apart, and the word appears in the account of those who cast Scripture behind their backs.
rows.anchor: النبذ أصله الطرح والانتباذ افتعال منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mary’s eastward withdrawal explains why Christians adopted the east as their direction of prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس إنما اتخذت النصارى المشرق قبلة لأنها انتبذت مكانا شرقيا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Mary withdrew to worship without distraction from people’s conversation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اتخذت مكانا تنفرد فيه للعبادة لئلا تشتغل بكلام الناس عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another view says she moved far enough away that her people could not see her.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تباعدت عن قومها حتى لا يرونها عن الأصم وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Mary may have sought privacy to comb her hair while sitting in the sun on a bitterly cold day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها تمنت أن تجد خلوة فتفلي رأسها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: God’s spirit sent to Mary is Gabriel; calling him spirit honors his spiritual nature and the possessive relation to God.
rows.anchor: يعني جبرائيل ع عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the spirit from which Christ was created appeared to Mary as a human; the author prefers Gabriel, citing the exegetes’ agreement.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم إن الروح الذي خلق منه المسيح تصور لها إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s conditional appeal means that a God-fearing man will recoil when she seeks refuge in God, so she warns him to leave.
rows.anchor: أن التقي إذا تعوذ بالرحمن منه ارتدع عما يسخط الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali explains that piety restrains a pious person from sin.
rows.anchor: علمت أن التقي ينهاه التقى عن المعصية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading treats her words as reproach: someone who looked at her and secluded himself with her was not truly pious.
rows.anchor: ما كنت تقيا حيث استحللت النظر إلي وخلوت بي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The promised pure boy is understood as a prophet.
rows.anchor: يريد نبيا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary explains that she has neither a husband nor sexual misconduct; ordinarily a child comes from one of those two routes.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالت ذلك لأن الولد في العادة يكون من إحدى هاتين الجهتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode supports the possibility of miracles for a nonprophet: Mary was not a prophet, yet saw Gabriel, conceived without intercourse, and received other signs.
rows.anchor: دلالة على جواز إظهار المعجزات لغير الأنبياء

rows.speaker: الجبائي وابنه
rows.claim: Those who deny miracles to nonprophets call these signs miracles of Zakariya instead.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي وابنه إنها معجزات لزكريا

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi calls them miracles of Jesus that preceded and established his prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال البلخي إنها معجزات لعيسى على سبيل الارهاص

rows.speaker: حمزة وحفص
rows.claim: They read nasy with an open n; the remaining readers use a kasra, with both forms meaning something insignificant and forgotten.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحفص نسيا بفتح النون والباقون نسيا بكسر النون

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والكوفة غير أبي بكر وسهل
rows.claim: These readers use min tahtiha with a kasra under the m; the others use the open reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ من تحتها بكسر الميم أهل المدينة والكوفة غير أبي بكر وسهل

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Nasy is a negligible thing easily forgotten, such as a sandal or whip; other lexicographers call it the least significant thing.
rows.anchor: النسي هو الشيء الحقير ينسى نحو النعل والسوط

rows.speaker: الشنفرى
rows.claim: Al-Shanfara’s poem uses nasy for a small, overlooked object that is searched for on the ground.
rows.anchor: كأن لها في الأرض نسيا تقصه على أمها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The caller from beneath Mary may be Gabriel or Jesus; some insist it must be Jesus because Gabriel would call from above.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التأويل لا يكون إلا عيسى ع ولا يكون جبرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors Jesus as the caller because he would most directly remove Mary’s grief; beneath can mean below or near, not necessarily the lower direction.
rows.anchor: والأشبه أن يكون المنادي لها عيسى فإنه أشد إزالة لما خامر قلبها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The variants of tasāqaṭ generally agree; the subject may be the palm, or the trunk with the palm omitted in the wording.
rows.anchor: وكلهم جعل فاعل الفعل الذي هو تساقط أو تساقط في رواية حفص النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min tahtiha can mean from beneath or in front of her, by analogy with the stream described as beneath her; the wording may name Jesus generally after a narrower reference.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن النهر محاذيا لهذه الجهة ولكن المعنى جعله دونك

rows.speaker: أوفى بن مطر
rows.claim: His line provides a poetic example of the tafaʿala form taking an object, supporting the grammar of tasāqaṭ.
rows.anchor: تخاطأت النبل أحشاءه وأخر يومي فلم يعجل

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: The verb tanāsānī in his verse witnesses transitive use of tafaʿala, with the sense of making someone forget.
rows.anchor: لعوب تناساني إذا قمت سربالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the y reading, the omitted subject may be the shaking because Mary was told to shake, or it may be the trunk.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء أمكن أن يكون فاعله الهز لأن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit falling from the trunk would resemble the unexpected provision Mary earlier found in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: مثل رزقها الذي كان يأتيها المحراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rutan can be a direct object, or a circumstantial accusative with the fruit understood; the tree’s mention licenses the omitted fruit.
rows.anchor: ويكون انتصاب رطب على الحال وجاز أن يضمر الثمر وإن لم يجر لها ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The b in shaking the trunk may be extra, as in a cited line, or may mean that the dates fall through the act of shaking.
rows.anchor: فأما الباء في قوله: { وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة } فيحتمل أمرين

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s line supports construing a noun with bi as the action by which something arrives.
rows.anchor: وصوح البقل نأآج تجيء به هيف يمانية في مرها نكب

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading yusaqitu means that the fruit falls gradually, supported by a verse from Dabi al-Burjumi.
rows.anchor: أما قراءة مسروق يساقط فإنه بمعنى يسقط شيئا بعد شيء

rows.speaker: طلحة بن سليمان
rows.claim: He reads jani with kasra on its jim by vowel harmony with the following kasra; Ibn Jinni compares similar sound patterns.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة طلحة رطبا جنيا فإنه اتبع كسرة الجيم كسرة النون

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: The unusual form tarayinna retains n in the jussive, a dialectal usage illustrated by a line from Abu al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: وأما ترين فهي شاذ لكنه جاء في لغة إثبات النون في الجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasiy means far away, as opposed to near.
rows.anchor: القصي البعيد والقاصي خلاف الداني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajaaha means labor drove Mary there; the verb may be formed by adding the hamza or by using bi, as in Zuhayr’s verse and Tamimi usage.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: تميم تقول ما أجاءك إلى هذا وما أمشاك إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sari means a flowing stream; jani means fruit picked or gathered.
rows.anchor: والسري النهر لأنه يسري بجريانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh and Najd differ in the vowel of qarri: Quraysh uses kasra in the verb, while Najd uses fatha.
rows.anchor: قررت به عينا أقر قرورا فهي لغة قريش

rows.speaker: ابن أخت جذيمة
rows.claim: His line glosses jani as gathered fruit, a harvest ready to be eaten.
rows.anchor: هذا جناي وخياره فيه إذ كل جان يده إلى فيه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Fari may derive from cutting leather neatly and then extend to lying; al-Zajjaj instead uses it of a remarkable, highly accomplished deed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم الفري مأخوذ من فرى الأديم إذا قطعه على وجه الإصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here kana means becoming or occurring, though the grammarian also allows it to be redundant; the line from al-Rabiʿ supports the first reading.
rows.anchor: كان هنا بمعنى الحدوث والوقوع والتقدير كيف نكلم من وجد في المهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel tells Mary that God’s creating a child without a husband is easy; Jesus will be a clear sign of his prophethood and her innocence, and a mercy guiding people.
rows.anchor: معناه ولنجعله علامة ظاهرة وآية باهرة للناس على نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’s creation was a settled decree already completed in God’s judgment.
rows.anchor: وكان خلق عيسى من غير ذكر أمرا كائنا مفروغا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary conceived Jesus and withdrew to a distant place, away from relatives through shame and fear of accusation.
rows.anchor: أي تنحت الحمل إلى مكان بعيد

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: One report says Gabriel took the edge of Mary’s garment and blew into it, and she conceived immediately.
rows.anchor: إن جبرائيل أخذ ردن قميصها بإصبعه فنفخ فيه

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Another report says Gabriel blew into the neckline; the fetus completed instantly, Mary felt the weight, and she left ashamed after her aunt failed to recognize her.
rows.anchor: تناول جيب مدرعتها فنفخ فيه نفخة فكمل الولد في الرحم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The interval from Mary’s withdrawal to conception was only an hour, inferred from the immediate sequence of the verbs.
rows.anchor: لم يكن بين الانتباذ والحمل إلا ساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labor drove Mary to the palm trunk, where she leaned for support; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi identify this as the known palm.
rows.anchor: فالتجأت إليها لتستند إليها عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mary saw a mound, climbed it quickly, and found a dry, frondless palm trunk; the definite article points to that known tree.
rows.anchor: نظرت مريم إلى أكمة فصعدت مسرعة إليها فإذا عليها جذع نخلة نخرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Nasy means something discarded and forgotten; another gloss is something not remembered or recognized.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شيئا لا يذكر ولا يعرف عن قتادة

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another gloss of nasy is a discarded menstrual cloth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حيضة ملقاة عن عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They say Gabriel called Mary from below, at the foot of the hill.
rows.anchor: وهو قول السدي وقتادة والضحاك أن المنادي جبرائيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن ووهب وسعيد بن جبير وابن زيد وابن جرير والجبائي
rows.claim: These authorities say Jesus called her from below.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ناداها عيسى عن مجاهد والحسن ووهب

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Mary wished for death because she feared God would be disobeyed through people’s accusations; another report says she had no perceptive righteous person to clear her.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع لأنها لم تر في قومها رشيدا ذا فراسة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The stream beneath Mary was restored by God so she could drink and cleanse herself after childbirth.
rows.anchor: قد جعل ربك تحت قدميك نهرا تشربين منه وتتطهرين من النفاس

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: One report says Jesus struck the ground with his foot, causing a spring to gush forth; other reports credit Gabriel or God directly.
rows.anchor: بل ضرب عيسى برجله فظهرت عين ماء تجري

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Dates are especially suitable food for a woman after childbirth, and God fed them to Mary during her postpartum period.
rows.anchor: لم تستشف النفساء بمثل الرطب أن الله أطعمه مريم في نفاسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruiting palm was a miracle because the tree was dry and it was winter; dates appeared at once instead of passing through blossom, unripe, and ripe stages.
rows.anchor: وكان في الشتاء فصار معجزة بخروج الرطب في غير أوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Mary struck a headless palm with her foot; it blossomed and bore fruit, though a palm without a crown does not normally fruit.
rows.anchor: والشجرة التي لا رأس لها لا تثمر في العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is told to eat the dates, drink the water, and be comforted; qarri ʿaynan can mean feel at ease or rejoice at seeing her child.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير وطيبي نفسا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation connects cool eyes with joyful tears, contrasted with the heat of tears from grief.
rows.anchor: لأن دمعة السرور باردة ودمعة الحزن حارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mary’s fast means a vow of silence, not merely abstaining from food.
rows.anchor: أي صمتا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The word fast can mean abstaining from food, drink, and speech.
rows.anchor: صوما أي إمساكا عن الطعام والشراب والكلام عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن زيد ووهب
rows.claim: Silence allows the child to speak and vindicate Mary’s innocence.
rows.anchor: وإنما أمرت الصمت ليكفيها الكلام ولدها بما يبرىء به ساحتها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Israelites could fast from speech until evening; Mary was permitted to state her vow and then say nothing further.
rows.anchor: وكان قد أذن لها أن تتكلم بهذا القدر ثم تسكت

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: God must have ordered Mary to vow silence, since commanding her to claim a vow she had not made would entail a lie.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يأمرها بأن تخبر بأنها نذرت ولم تنذر

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: The people call the birth unprecedented and astounding because no woman before Mary had given birth without a man.
rows.anchor: قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes fari as a shameful falsehood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمرا قبيحا منكرا من الافتراء وهو الكذب عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وكعب وابن زيد والمغيرة بن شعبة
rows.claim: Aaron was a righteous Israelite, so sister of Aaron means Mary resembled him in piety; a report says forty thousand mourners at his funeral bore his name.
rows.anchor: هارون هذا كان رجلا صالحا في بني إسرائيل ينسب إليه كل من عرف بالصلاح

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: A second view says Aaron was Mary’s paternal half-brother, known for good conduct.
rows.anchor: أن هارون كان أخاها لأبيها ليس من أمها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: A third view identifies Aaron as Moses’s brother and calls Mary his sister by descent, like saying brother of Tamim.
rows.anchor: أن هارون أخو موسى ع فنسبت إليه لأنها من ولده

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A fourth view identifies Aaron as a notorious immoral man and treats the phrase as calling Mary his counterpart.
rows.anchor: أنه كان رجلا فاسقا مشهورا بالعهر والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people invoke Mary’s good father and chaste mother as evidence against her alleged misconduct.
rows.anchor: ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the palm as a barniya variety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن تلك النخلة كانت برنية.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report identifies the palm as the ajwa variety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت عجوة وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله ع.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The cradle can mean the lap or breast where Mary raised the infant, since no separate cradle had been prepared.
rows.anchor: وكان المهد حجر أمه الذي تربيه فيه إذ لم تكن هيأت له مهدا عن قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The people were angered by Mary’s gesture, calling it more insulting than her alleged fornication; when Jesus spoke they recognized the gravity of the event.
rows.anchor: لسخريتها بنا أشد علينا من زناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus begins by declaring himself God’s servant, refuting claims of divinity that God knew some would make about him.
rows.anchor: قدم إقراره بالعبودية ليبطل به قول من يدعي له الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words about receiving the Book and becoming a prophet mean God decreed those gifts for Jesus.
rows.anchor: أي حكم لي بإتيان الكتاب والنبوة

rows.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
rows.claim: One view says God completed Jesus’s reason as a child, sent him to people, and made him accountable as a prophet; his speech was a miracle.
rows.anchor: أكمل عقله في صغره وأرسله إلى عباده وكان نبيا مبعوثا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: One report says Jesus spoke when he was forty days old.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كلمهم وهو ابن أربعين يوما عن وهب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that Jesus spoke on the day he was born.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يوم ولد عن ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes the verbs future tense, saying Jesus will receive the Book and prophethood; this speech itself vindicated Mary.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك معجزة لمريم ع على براءة ساحتها
